references.text: Jethro's original advice to Moses that judges should judge the people at all times and bring difficult cases to Moses, which is now put into practice.
Moses recounts how judges were instructed to judge fairly and bring difficult cases to him.
Instructions to bring difficult legal cases to the priests and judges for decision, reflecting the principle of hierarchical judicial resolution.
Jehoshaphat organized a legal system with judges in all cities and a higher court in Jerusalem for difficult cases, based on the same principle Moses established.
The apostles delegated tasks to the seven so they could focus on prayer and the ministry of the word, similar to the principle of delegating responsibility that Moses practiced.
Describes the same sequence of events where 18:13 presents the problem of overload which 18:26 resolves through delegation.
Illustrates the same legal principle: difficult cases requiring God's decision must be brought to Moses.
Highlights Moses' role as mediator: he receives the people's answer (19:8) and their difficult cases (18:26) for further handling with God.
